items.author: hwchase17
items.how: 1) You write the request in Slack and attach briefs. 2) Each Slack thread gets its own sandbox (an isolated, disposable virtual computer) where the agent keeps the project between messages. 3) The model makes the creative calls and everything is produced as code (HTML/CSS, animations, chart specs), then rendered to files; the agent looks at its own renders to fix them. 4) Its skills (procedure files it reads when needed) hold LangChain's design principles plus guardrails against AI slop. 5) For big jobs (a launch film takes hours) it acts as a chief of staff: it runs asynchronous subagents in parallel, shows the plan and progress in the thread, and asks for approval before shipping; several…
items.title: Content Studio: LangChain's design agent, driven from Slack
items.try: Apache 2.0 license, Python 3.12+, can be tried locally without keys per the README; Slack deployment via Managed Deep Agents (paid LangSmith offering). Star count not read.
items.what: An agent that lives in Slack: anyone at the company asks it for a visual (video, social graphic, slide deck, recreated UI image) the way they would ask a designer. Put simply, a Canva plus junior designer that knows your brand and answers in a Slack thread.
items.who: The design team was buried under small repetitive requests. Published results: 3,000+ assets, 80+ decks, three in four requests from outside marketing, median cost per request down from about $8 to about $0.50. A textbook business agent: a real ops workflow, a clear architecture (main agent + subagents + sandbox + skills) and numbers. Key lesson: delete the rules that made up for model weaknesses once models improve; keep the principles.

items.author: claudeai
items.how: A connector usually relies on MCP (Model Context Protocol, a standard plug that lets an AI talk to software). A skill is a folder of instructions and scripts that Claude loads only when the task calls for it. The plugin bundles both so that in one click Claude can access the tool and knows how to use it well. The catalog mixes Claude Code plugins (PR review, LSP, security) and Cowork plugins (Atlassian, Slack, Figma...).
items.title: Claude Plugins: connectors and skills combined in one format
items.try: Available on Free, Pro, Max and Ultra; Team and Enterprise coming soon. 10,000+ plugins announced. Site not reachable (claude.ai/plugins), details from the tweet and the claude.com/plugins page.
items.what: There is now one way to add a capability to Claude: a plugin, which can contain a connector (access to an external tool such as Slack, Jira or Supabase), a skill (a written way of working), or both. Put simply, an app store for Claude.
items.who: Before, you had to plug in a connector on one side and write a skill on the other. It is the simplest building block to equip an ops agent (CRM, Notion, Slack) without coding.

items.author: claudeai
items.how: 1) Classifiers (small models that screen each request one by one) miss attacks split into many harmless-looking requests. 2) EFS adds monitoring that looks for patterns across many requests. 3) Inputs and outputs are written to your own storage (S3 or Google Cloud Storage), encrypted with your keys, then deleted on Anthropic's side. 4) Only the automated monitoring accesses them (no human review, no training). 5) When it finds a risk you get a Safety Case (without the content) that can feed your SIEM (security monitoring tool). It also flags agents that go beyond the user's intent.
items.title: Enterprise Frontier Safeguards: misuse detection without keeping your data
items.try: Public beta for eligible customers on Claude Platform, AWS, Bedrock and Google Cloud; Microsoft Foundry coming soon. Storage is billed by your cloud provider.
items.what: An Anthropic option for companies that want ZDR (zero data retention: neither Anthropic nor the cloud keeps prompts and outputs) while keeping misuse monitoring. Put simply: your logs stay in your own vault, but a security robot can still read them.
items.who: Regulated industries (healthcare, finance, legal) that held back on frontier models for lack of guarantees. Developed with 100+ customers (Stripe, Salesforce and Bridgewater were in the private beta).

items.author: geoffreyhuntley
items.how: XNU is built from Apple's published sources and runs as a kernel module (xnu.ko); a small interface module (fki.ko) lends it Linux's memory, timers, files, network and GPU.
items.title: xnulinux: running macOS inside Linux
items.what: Loads the macOS kernel (XNU) as a Linux kernel module, without a hypervisor (the software that runs virtual machines): Safari, Finder and the Dock run next to Linux programs on an ARM machine.
items.who: An impressive but very low-level feat. Skip unless curious.
